topic.title: Does a UPI payment above ₹2,000 at a shop now cost the customer extra

title: Shopkeeper says UPI above ₹2,000 costs extra? Here is who really pays
description: The talk at the counter: pay by UPI above ₹2,000 and you pay a fee. The proposed 0.4% merchant fee is charged to the shop, not you, and it has been put off until after Diwali. Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Has a shop refused your UPI?

lines.text: The shopkeeper says paying by UPI above ₹2,000 now costs me extra!
Actually, that fee is called MDR. It is charged to the shop, not to you.
The plan is a fee of 0.4% on shop payments above ₹2,000.
So on a bill of ₹5,000, the shop's bank keeps ₹20. Your bill stays ₹5,000.
Sending money to a friend stays free. And the shop fee is a cost for the shop, not a charge on you.
And right now, it isn't even live. It has been put off until after Diwali.
So the extra charge was never mine to pay.
Next time the shopkeeper says that, you'll know who pays.

Story current. Disclaimer ends description. Minor: 'the shop's bank keeps Rs 20' simplifies MDR shared among banks/PSPs/apps; small-merchant and Rs 5 essential-sector exemptions not mentioned.
